0.content:
Mavuika could not have foreseen the Traveler five hundred years ago, but after one moment's thought she made them part of her plan, partly because they reminded her of herself. She commissioned Xilonen to forge them an Ancient Name, the first ever for an outlander: Tumaini, "hope". Because of their resistance to the Abyss, only the Traveler could join her final descent into the Night Kingdom, where together they destroyed Gosoythoth. She says Tumaini and Kiongozi are now linked and will live on together. After the war she told the Traveler she had been lost and that their curiosity, exploration and dedication to others showed her the way.

She asked the Traveler to introduce her to the other Archons, and warned them before Snezhnaya to prepare for trouble with the Fatui. In 6.6 she handed them the Pyro Gnosis at the sealed Sumeru border, saying their coming was one of the main reasons she agreed. They absorbed it, perhaps through their mastery of Pyro, so it could pass Irminsul's barrier. "You might not be recorded in the Ley Lines, but you're still our Tumaini."

1.content:
The First of the Fatui Harbingers came to the Stadium in 5.0, accused Mavuika of failing the oath sworn five hundred years ago, and challenged her for the Pyro Gnosis. She left a searing wound on his chest and felt she was fighting "the pinnacle of human strength". He escaped in a mist from the Masters of the Night-Wind, later traced to Ororon. In 5.1 she rejected his plan to rewrite Natlan's ley lines, which would erase its history like using the Gnosis. He then accepted her plan and lent her his soldiers. After Gosoythoth fell and Ronova came for Mavuika's life at Ochkanatlan, Capitano took her place and fused himself with the Lord of the Night. He argued Natlan still needed its leader, and she came to agree.

She found out he had given up on the Gnosis after losing to her, out of respect for her victory, though she still feared the Tsaritsa might send another Harbinger. She never saw his face. At the ceremony for the fallen she publicly honoured him as a Harbinger who fought for Natlan and protected her. "For him, I suspect the past five hundred years felt endless... I have great respect for warriors like him." She wished she could have shared grilled meat and travel stories with him and the Traveler.

2.content:
The Masters of the Night-Wind's great shaman is the only person who "inappropriately" knocks on Mavuika's door in her quiet hours, perhaps for the drink, perhaps because they suit each other as drinking buddies. Mavuika says people find Citlali strange, but she ignores trivia and is always there when it counts. Mavuika keeps certain things from her because Citlali tunnel-visions into trouble, but Citlali sees right through her. Citlali, for her part, complains that a visit from Mavuika turned out to be bragging.

Citlali tracked down the traitor who helped Capitano (her "grandson" Ororon), read the Wayob's warning about Xbalanque, and led the Traveler to Ochkanatlan when Mavuika went to die.

3.content:
Mavuika wanted a vehicle that was fast, armoured, able to cross cliffs, water and air, explosive enough to be a weapon and summonable with a flick of her wrist. She brought the demand to Xilonen of the Children of Echoes, along with Source Mechanisms she had scoured from Natlan and blueprints she had copied by hand from devices the ancient dragons built against the Abyss. Many explosions later, the two produced a Pyro-compatible prototype. Xilonen declined the test rides, claiming she had "forgotten to make a second helmet". Mavuika praises her as a master who never backs away from a challenge.

Xilonen says it took three months and counts the Flamestrider among Mavuika's ridiculous commissions, ahead of heat-proof swords and special sunglasses, and well ahead of forging an Ancient Name for an outlander. Xilonen has refused every Flamestrider Grand Prix proposal.

4.content:
Mavuika's mother Haumia was bold and reckless; her unnamed father was learned and taciturn. The two clashed until their curious, fearless daughter became a bridge between them. Her younger sister Hine was mischievous, quiet by turns and rarely obedient, and Mavuika passed on to her everything she learned. Her Yumkasaur Hitata leapt into her arms whenever he saw her, and Hine would jealously do the same. When Mavuika announced her plan, Haumia gave her blessing and Hine promised to find a way to meet again.

Once Hine asked how they could be sure every Pyro Archon would protect them; their father said ordinary people need no such guarantee and told her to ask her sister. Mavuika only smiled and hugged her. Hine grew up to become an architect who helped rebuild the Scions, but little of her life survives. Hine left her architecture manual, with a paper frog folded long ago, with a family she had helped, to be passed to Mavuika on her return; it reached her. In the final battle Hine appeared to Mavuika in the Night Kingdom as the child she remembered, and Mavuika told her she had received both. Afterwards Mavuika wrote her a letter saying Natlan was at peace, and burned it to send it.

5.content:
After the cataclysm, Mavuika's people estimated that the Night Kingdom would fall to the Abyss within five hundred years. Her answer was a plan: the tribes would rebuild, the Wayob would choose six heroes carrying the old heroes' Ancient Names, and she would return to lead one final war. Because Natlan has no god to extend a human life, she placed her life in the Sacred Flame, dying before her time in order to return. Warriors brought her their most precious belongings as fuel full of Contending Fire. She gave each a hot drink and listened to the story behind every item, so their memories would reach the future.

Few asked about her own stories. Those who did heard about her parents, Hine and two mischievous Yumkasaurs, and then: "All of it ceased to be important the moment we decided on this plan, even me." The plan nearly failed because the Night Kingdom's decay cut the Sacred Flame off from the Wayob, so the new heroes were never told what their Names were for.

6.content:
Mavuika refused every suggestion to use the Pyro Gnosis, before the cataclysm and after, because rewriting the ley lines would erase Natlan's history. In 6.6 (Song of the Welkin Moon Act X), Nicole of the Hexenzirkel arranged a meeting at the sealed Sumeru border. Nahida appeared as a memory, since Dottore lurked in Irminsul. Mavuika guessed the request herself and handed the Gnosis over, saying she had always toyed with giving it to someone who needed it more. Nahida used it to burn the corrupted Irminsul. Afterward the Gnosis could not be found, and Mavuika had already sensed its loss.

She told the guilt-stricken Nahida that this time there was to be no "returning", only "giving", and suggested the loss might be a knock-on effect on a strand of fate. Then she took Nahida and the Traveler out to enjoy the sunshine. As of 7.1 she holds no Gnosis.

7.content:
Xbalanque's rules gave Mavuika a single chance to wield the power of Ronova, Shade of Death, at the price of her fated death. She used it in 5.1 to break the Abyss invasion. After the final battle, Citlali and the Traveler found her at Ochkanatlan before Ronova's watching rift, ready to pour her life back into the Sacred Flame to strengthen the weakened Lord of the Night. Ronova ordered the Lord of the Night to kill her, but the Lord hesitated: someone else was coming. Capitano offered his cursed, undying life instead, forcing Ronova to choose between breaking her own curse and a paradox. Ronova upheld the curse, and Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night.

In 7.1, hearing that the Traveler had taken Ronova out in Snezhnaya, Mavuika said she had never liked her either.

8.comment: Mavuika: The Six Heroes of Natlan
8.content: The modern heroes of her plan: Kinich (Malipo, "cost"), Mualani (Umoja, unity), Iansan (Uwezo), Xilonen (Baraka), Ororon (Bidii) and Chasca (Vuka). Kachina was the hero whose loss in the Night Kingdom set Chapter V in motion. Mavuika values Malipo for asking unwelcome questions. She says Mualani inherited Tupac's Name with a different temperament but the same willingness to risk everything for a friend. She calls Ororon lava under ice, and wants Natlan gentler for Chasca. She blames herself for Kachina's scars.

9.comment: Mavuika: The Heroes of the Cataclysm
9.content: Five hundred years ago Tenoch gathered warriors from each tribe against the black tide, and Mavuika joined them as Archon. She grew up with Burkina, studied under the trainer Sundjatta and wrestled Wanjiru, always winning except once, days before she became Archon. In the "Sunset" short, the survivors toasted her plan the night before their last stand. She led them out with the words that Natlan would remember the day. Menilek and Sundjatta fell, and the dying Tupac carried her to the throne of the Sacred Flame. In her dream-journey the names of Atea, Tenoch, Sundjatta, Burkina and Wanjiru say farewell to her one by one.

10.content: In her Story Quest the Wayob warned that the first Pyro Archon was returning. Mavuika turned the obsolete Pilgrimage into a friendly tournament as bait and toured the tribes with the Traveler, testing Iansan's obstacle course and eating half a restaurant's meat. Kinich won. She found Xbalanque riding in the sickly boy Mausau. Ronova had granted him one day to see whether Natlan had won. They duelled as spirits at the Temple of Souls until the flames died, and he named her the narrow victor. She declined his reward, a brief return of someone from the Night Kingdom, saying the past should stay a memory. He had known her answer and brought her loved ones' voices anyway. She gave him a Flamestrider ride across Natlan before he left; Mausau woke inspired to train.

11.comment: Mavuika: Kachina and the Night Kingdom Rescue
11.content: In 5.0 Kachina did not return through the Ode of Resurrection, and Mavuika could find no trace of her Ancient Name. She suspended the Pilgrimage. Privately, she said it was a lost cause anyway: Contending Fire was running out and the tribes had to keep their strength. She sent the Traveler, Mualani and Chasca into the Night Kingdom with a Spiritspeaker Stone. When the Abyss trapped them, she burned every keepsake she had kept for five centuries to bring them back. Then she told them Natlan might have less than a year.

12.comment: Mavuika: The Final Battle and Gosoythoth
12.content: With the Traveler's Name forged, Mavuika roused the Stadium and took them both into the Night Kingdom. She split from the Traveler to strike the enemy's core. Hine's presence came to support her; the Traveler cleared the nests helped by the dead of Natlan. Gosoythoth became a sword-wielding dragon and cast Mavuika into a void that tried to make her doubt. She answered that her fate was to end the war, and even when the Sacred Flame went out, the people's support carried them to victory.

13.content: As a small child Mavuika was proud when her father won the Pilgrimage. His team won its Night Warden War after three days and nights, but three of the seven fell, him among them. The Ode of Resurrection reversed only the killing wound, so he came home covered in injuries, unable to stand. It was the first time she felt death's gaze. She held back tears and gripped his hand. He told her everyone fears death, but some step forward to protect something. She answered: "Since we're forced to fight this war, then I wish to put an end to it." Her parents nodded instead of laughing, and the gods' gaze came to rest on her. She has never doubted the trust in their eyes.

14.comment: Mavuika: Barbatos and the Mare Jivari
14.content: In 5.8, while Venti holidayed in Natlan, he quietly worked with Mavuika: she opened a rift between the Mare Jivari's echo and the true Mare Jivari so he could bring back every soul that wished to return home. Afterward, at Me & Dew on Tete Isle, she praised his toast "for happiness and freedom", invited him to the rowdy tribal banquets, and promised extra barrels of Aphimead and the new "Quenepacano" for a joint Mondstadt-Natlan banquet. Venti in turn admires the "god-like feat" of her heroes and teases her with old epics.

15.comment: Mavuika: Mavuika and the Other Archons
15.content: Before Natlan's war she admitted the Traveler probably knew the other Archons better than she did, and planned to strengthen ties once it ended. Ei remembers a Khaenri'ah battlefield scorched by her fury and wants a sparring match. Zhongli praises a leader who wields time and history as weapons. Nahida says many Natlanese plan to visit Sumeru. Neuvillette calls the dragon-seized Authority a sin but is in no hurry to act. Mavuika hopes Ei's love of hot springs will open their next conversation. Grand Master Varka came to see her and ended up in a drinking contest at the Stadium; he forgot why he came, and each tells it differently.

16.content: Mavuika rates puzzles for quality, difficulty and reasonability and re-solves old ones under self-imposed limits: placing pieces face-down, or fixing one part of a metal or knot puzzle to the table. She once published her catalog through the Speaker's Chamber, but sellers abused her endorsement. Now a hobbyist may view it only after solving a random puzzle from her collection. She learned rock climbing by memorising every move and having a Kamera record her failures, until she and her coach became fellow enthusiasts. She paints when duty allows and does Akademiya puzzle collections before bed.

17.comment: Mavuika: The Office of Pyro Archon
17.content: Any Natlanese who proves themselves the mightiest warrior of the era in a Pilgrimage can become Pyro Archon. The rules, the Ode of Resurrection and the divine name Haborym go back to Xbalanque's bargain with Ronova two thousand years ago. Every Archon leaves knowledge and memories in the Sacred Flame; the flood can shake a successor's sense of self, so Mavuika left them the words "Before you become one with flame, be proud of who you are now." Other Archons held the throne while she slept.

18.content: After the 7.1 Archon Quest, strange marks appeared over the Celestial Nails across Teyvat. At the Stadium the Traveler found Mavuika staring at Natlan's, calling its position precarious; as Paimon noted, Natlan's hangs right beside where people live. She congratulated them on taking out Ronova and said the Heavenly Principles have always used Natlan as a tool against the Abyss, so whatever comes, the Traveler will not be to blame. She told her people to watch for danger.

19.content: In a limited-time web event (December 2024), the Speaker's Chamber warned people not to worry about loud noises during the Archon's training. Mavuika rode the Flamestrider over a cliff, free-climbed the Stadium's highest cliffs to catch the sunset, and surfed whitewater beyond what People of the Springs surfers attempt. Then she began planning a harder version. Onlookers included Kachina, Xilonen, Iansan, Kinich and Ajaw, Chasca, Mualani, Citlali, Ororon and the Captain.

20.content: After the war Mavuika restarted the Bloomflower Trials, an old contest suspended after its founders warped it. When the sick boy Milray feared the crystals because the qucusaur spirit Antu said they beguile hearts, everyone agreed to stage a story in which the crystals were stopped by a force of good. Mavuika pretended she could not control them so that Ifa and Antu could "save the day".
